findings.title: Same concurrent-delete NPE risk remains in sibling getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: getSubGroupsCount() was fixed to null-check the result of modelSupplier.get() before calling getSubGroupsCount() on it (lines 272-276), but the three overloaded getSubGroupsStream methods (lines 254-257, 259-263, 265-269) still do `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without any null check. modelSupplier.get() calls getGroupModel() -> cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId()), which can legitimately return null if the group is concurrently deleted — exactly the race this PR is meant to fix. Calling getSubGroupsStream(...) on that null result will still NPE, so the reported concurrency bug can still occur through these paths even after this patch, leaving the fix incomplete.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() now can return null, a contract change that may just relocate the NPE
findings.body: The fix changes getSubGroupsCount() to return null when the underlying group model can no longer be resolved (concurrently deleted), instead of throwing NPE. This is a behavior/contract change for an interface method that previously always returned a non-null Long in the success case. Callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount (representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())) tolerate null, but other call sites across the codebase that unconditionally unbox or otherwise assume a non-null Long were not audited/updated in this PR, so the underlying race may simply surface as an NPE somewhere else instead of being eliminated.

findings.title: Background reader thread is never joined before asserting on caughtExceptions, creating a race in the regression test
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, a background Thread is started (line 139) that loops calling groups() until deletedAll is set to true. After deleting all groups and setting deletedAll.set(true) (line 155), the test immediately asserts assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) (line 157) without calling Thread.join(). The background thread only checks the flag at the top of its loop, so an exception produced by a request that is in-flight (or about to run) when the flag flips may be recorded into caughtExceptions after the assertion has already executed, letting a real regression pass unnoticed (false negative). Additionally, since the thread is never joined, it can keep running past the end of the test method, continuing to call the admin client/HTTP client after the test's injected resources (managedRealm, adminClient) may be torn down, risking flakiness or interference with subsequent tests.
